6.t: Henderson's education and why he was aloof
6.s: Henderson was well schooled, with a science background, which made him less of a mixer, though he later shot pool with the band at the Rhythm Club.
6.q: on, because he used to come to the Rhythm Club. We used to shoot pool together in the morning, you know, after work. Yeah.

6.t: Fletcher as easygoing perfectionist; playing an opera singer's accompaniment
6.s: Henderson was easygoing and brilliant; at Hollywood Gardens he sat down and played an opera star's arias on piano when the band couldn't read her music.
6.q: Rudy Wiedoft was a saxophone player, one of the original saxophone players, I'll put it that way, because he was way back, 1913, '14, '15, those days, you know. And he was on the opposite stand for about a week or so. And lo and behold, the featured singer was an opera star. That's the type of…

6.t: John Hammond's theater scheme and the band's walkout
6.s: After Connie's Inn, Hammond's idea of opening a theater failed when half the outspoken band showed up, because they disliked Hammond; Procope laments the TV tribute and Hammond's Goodman devotion.
6.q: When Fletcher's -- well, this is the only time, when we left Connie's Inn, and we were, you know, sort of knocking around, and then John Hammond came up with this idea of getting this theater down on 12th Street someplace, and he opened this theater, and then he had -- well, I guess on the surface…

79.t: Henderson as a strict musician like Mr. Langford
79.s: Thomas says Henderson, in his teacher's mold, was easygoing except about music, wanting players to interpret rather than just blow.
79.q: Not with music. He wasn't easy going at all with music. And I appreciated him very much for that so we happened little saying, to say left hand corner. I'll wait and leave an interpretation. Anybody can blow horn but interpret what you were saying. So, that was a tremendous thing for us.

79.t: Henderson as a leader; overconfidence and John Hammond
79.s: Thomas says Henderson was strict about the music but too sure of himself, and the band's momentum was lost when John Hammond's connection with Benny Goodman took over.
79.q: Well, that could be a point but, you know, when you do a lot of things, you've got to have somebody to take your care of other things. If you sit here in your home and you're write for 12 hours a night, somebody has got to take care of the other side of it. That's where he was -- very strict about…

422.t: Fletcher Henderson as a bandleader and businessman
422.s: Henderson was not an effective leader and lacked a manager like Irving Mills or Glaser.
422.ch: Henderson, Goodman and the swing era
422.q: No. He wasn’t. Not at all. No. He just wasn’t. They talk about that accident that happened, the car accident, which after that he seemed very aloof and not really interested much in promoting the band very much. But even before that I kind of wonder how much of a leader he really was. I mean he…

366.s: Sol describes Henderson as gracious and recalls playing Goodman's Henderson arrangements.
366.ch: Sidemen, Steve Allen and the Goodman film
366.q: A very fine gentleman. A wonderful man, a wonderful pianist, and one of the highlights of my career because I knew about his music with Benny Goodman and he actually took me under his wing. He was very nice to me, and very warm and gracious to me. And every time I played with Fletcher Henderson I…

80.t: Fletcher Henderson's easygoing, easily used character
80.s: Autrey felt sorry for Henderson, who went along with whatever people wanted and was taken advantage of.
80.ch: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
80.q: He was. He was. He was very easy, you know, he was one of those types -- I did, I felt sorry for him because he was -- well all right. Yes. Okay, you know. He's always -- always so willing to -- I'm with you, whatever you say. If that's the way you want it. Okay. Everything's all right with me. You…

406.t: Fletcher Henderson as a man, and learning clarinet from Buster Bailey's book
406.s: Henderson was a quiet, kind man who laughed when Barefield messed up Buster Bailey's clarinet parts and encouraged him, which made him a real clarinetist.
406.q: Well, I knew him, knew of Fletcher, but I really met him when I joined the band in California. And Fletcher Henderson was one of the nicest men you ever met. He was a very passive type of a person and very quiet. I remember when I -- this is really where I got together on my clarinet, in Fletcher's…

67.t: Rehearsing and working with Fletcher Henderson
67.s: He rehearsed a long time with Fletcher Henderson, a carefree man who never reaped the harvest of Goodman's success, before Henderson died.
67.ch: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
67.q: Well, that was during the same time yes. I rehearsed with Fletcher with -- for quite a long time, but he didn't -- he didn't -- he was supposed to go into the Savoy, that's when he died. He didn't make it.

68.t: Fletcher Henderson's undisciplined band and the Steel Pier
68.s: Henderson never had a full band on the bandstand; stories of the Atlantic City Steel Pier.
68.q: Then he's the one told me Fletcher wasn't a good business manager and they never made time. You know, he hardly ever got his whole band on the bandstand at one time. Now, I understand they played at Atlantic City Steel Pier and it was hard -- see, that hadn't had no black bands in there. So they…

89.t: Fletcher Henderson's mistakes, and the band leaving Chick Webb on the road
89.s: Fletcher could not play after Benny Goodman performed his arrangements first, and the band once left an unpaid Chick Webb by the roadside.
89.q: I don't think anybody that you know now, but I did some of the arranging for the band in those days, too, as well as the Apollo Theater. That's about as much as I can elaborate on Snowden. I think it's worth mentioning about another one of our great leaders. I mentioned his name before. I've been…

28.t: Fletcher Henderson and the aloofness of big stars
28.s: He loved Fletcher Henderson but explains how great bandleaders were hard to approach, with sidemen like Sonny Greer as gatekeepers.
28.ch: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
28.q: Now, Sonny Greer was the one who'd get you. "Cut it. Jack. a little) Sonny Greer was the one, you know, everybody was around Duke, "Oh, Mr. Ellington." "Oh, Mr. Fletcher Henderson." You'd be back there and it was hard to get to him. And if he wanted to stop, he wouldn't have time. Because these…

0.t: Horace Henderson's treatment of Fletcher, and his absence at the funeral
0.s: Horace borrowed Fletcher's car, took his music and was missing at the funeral; Dance later found him playing a hotel lounge in Colorado.
0.ch: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
0.q: Horace just treated Fletcher so bad when he came here. He brought a little group here from out of -- from out of Ohio. And Fletcher, you know, he was a good piano player, and Fletcher would loan him his car, would run off with Fletcher's car, and he stole a lot of themusic and all like that. And…

382.t: Earl Hines, Claude Hopkins and Fletcher Henderson
382.s: She heard Hines on remote broadcasts and talks about Benny Goodman hiring Fletcher Henderson.
382.ch: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
382.q: So that's when Benny went out and hired Fletcher Henderson and you know, arrangers there. Because they was really breathing down Benny's neck. I mean, Benny is the band leader, it was a good band. But we've been listening to some good music before we heard that broadcast. I know that Benny was with…

758.s: Roy discusses Fletcher's lack of business sense, recording deals for Moe Gale, Horace's role, and hard keys.
758.q: : but I was the only one and I turned out to be the rebel, and everybody was looking at me with the fisheye, so I had to go along with it. For Moe Gale, you know. It was ridiculous, the prices they wanted us to record for, you know.

70.t: Fletcher Henderson as a quiet leader
70.s: Henderson was a milquetoast leader whose men were habitually late and he said nothing.
70.ch: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
70.q: Fletcher was a very quiet guy. He was another milquetoast guy, type of guy. You know, the guys used to just run over him, --

234.t: Fletcher Henderson's poverty and Willard Alexander
234.s: Gil says Henderson died poor while Benny Goodman made millions, and is angry with Willard Alexander.
234.ch: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
234.q: He's Benny Goodman (NCA?). He had his own band and he was with the band a lot when they were popular. Now he gave them the name 'King of Swing', right? So, I remember Willard Alexander out of all the people I've met in the business, he's one of the meanest men I've met you know. He really is. There…

418.t: Fletcher Henderson's stars and why big bands cannot feature everyone
418.s: Asked about Louis's complaint that Henderson did not feature him, Dickenson says a big band full of stars cannot distribute solos and lists Henderson's players.
418.ch: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
418.q: Well, that's the trouble with having a big band with a lot of stars in it. You understand? When you've got a band with a lot of stars, you try to distribute them out, you know... It makes it... You'd have to play all night long to get everybody featured. That's the trouble with being in a big band.…

96.t: Fletcher Henderson's arrangements and Goodman's success
96.s: Johnston notes Henderson's arrangements made Goodman rich while Henderson died poor.
96.q: That's true. Well that's terrible because he was so helpful and Benny Goodman's success really were with those arrangements.

387.s: Fletcher Henderson's wife copied for Benny; Sauter's respect for Fletcher; Fletcher's band early in the evening.
387.q: Teddy Wilson; wonderful, a lovely human being. And Fletcher, a very kind human being. Fletcher's wife I used to--Fletcher's wife used to copy from Benny and I'd run things down there at three thirty, four o'clock in the morning and never a problem.

389.t: Trumbauer fronting, Ludwig and arrangement swaps with Fletcher
389.s: Trumbauer stood in front while Ludwig still counted off; Blue Room and possibly Stampede went to Henderson, and he later arranged for Fletcher.
389.ch: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
389.q: Oh, shortly after. It wasn't too long. Another thing that was done, that seemed to bug some of the guys, the [disc-ers] discos today, is while we were there, and as I say, we were short on arrangements, at least they figured we were, I guess -- maybe it was Ludwig, it could have been Horvath but…

97.t: Henderson's band at the top; Whiteman's praise; strict inspections
97.s: Henderson's band is the top band, Paul Whiteman admires it, and Henderson inspects the men each night.
97.q: Well, Duke came to town. And he was playing at the Kentucky Club, 48th Street and Broadway. Now, you know, in those days, it wasn't so many musicians, and Fletcher's band was the top band. And Paul Whitman had been named just a couple of years ago the King of Jazz. He was a violinist. And Paul…

473.t: Fletcher Henderson asks him to stay; Cab sends money anyway
473.s: Fletcher offered recording work and a welcome back; Jones said he owed Fletcher $200, and Cab sent about $300 to settle it. Jones praises Smack as an easy leader, in contrast to Horace.
473.ch: Leaving Stuff Smith; Benny Carter and Fletcher Henderson
473.q: I said, "Fletcher, I think I'm going with Cab, because he offered a little more bread, you know, and I think I'll go over there for a while, you know." He says, "No, stay here. I'm doing some things with Benny Goodman and you can be in on some of the recordings and stuff," and he says, "What the…
